description: Leartech preset for Go services. Layer on top of default.json — adds groups for the leartech-go-runtime base image, internal Go libraries, the Go toolchain, and security-driven bumps.

packageRules.description: Only propose Go dependency updates that stay source-compatible with this repo's go directive, so a bump never arrives un-mergeable (needing a go-line bump to accept).

Auto-merge leartech-go-runtime image bumps as soon as they land. 'at any time' overrides default Monday-only schedule — internal lib, low risk, but consumers can be blocked on it (e.g. fleet Go-1.26 bump 2026-05-07).

Keep the go.mod toolchain directive current. Renovate proposes toolchain bumps by default; group + auto-merge them 'at any time' because a stale toolchain is what turns every repo's govulncheck gate red at once when a Go stdlib advisory drops (seen fleet-wide 2026-10-08: go1.26.6 -> go1.27.2).

Auto-merge leartech-{go,bus}-common + generated leartech-{go,bus}-packages/* as soon as they land. 'at any time' overrides the default Monday-only schedule because internal libs may need to flow within hours — and the go-common release fires a trigger-renovate job precisely so that flow starts within minutes. That fast flow is kept deliberately. What was MISSING was a ceiling on how MANY consumer repos open their bump PR at the same instant: with no limit, one tag opened a PR in every repo at once and every .lighthouse pipeline started together, swamping Tekton. The fix is the fleet-wide prConcurrentLimit/prHourlyLimit/branchConcurrentLimit in default.json, which staggers the SAME fast flow into waves the cluster can absorb — the trigger still does its job, the bumps still land within hours, they just arrive a few repos at a time rather than all at once.

Security-driven bumps (OSV/GitHub advisories) open immediately, overriding the Monday-only default schedule, so a vulnerable dependency is not left red for up to a week. Grouped so the fix PR is one unit.
